Your Skin and Hair

Oxford Read and Discover · Level 2 · Your Body · Pages 4–5

🔒 New Words 1 · Listen & Fill 2 · Write 3 · Present 4 · Mind Map

★ New Words

🔒 This part is for the teacher.

Teach these words before the listening task. Press 🔊 to hear the word (American English). Show the picture, read the meaning, then read the example.

skin

noun

The outside cover of your body.

“You have skin everywhere on your body.”

hair

noun

Thin lines that grow on your head and body.

“Hair grows out of your skin.”

body

noun

All of you, from your head to your feet.

“Protect your body!”

dirt

noun

Something that makes things not clean, like mud.

“Skin stops dirt getting into your body.”

sweat

noun

Water that comes out of your skin when you are hot.

“Your skin makes sweat when you’re hot.”

grow

verb

To get bigger or longer.

“Hair grows out of your skin.”

stand up

verb

To go up straight.

“Hair on your arms stands up when you’re cold.”

rainy

adjective

When water falls from the sky.

“Skin stops water getting in when it’s rainy.”

wash

verb

To make something clean with water and soap.

“Wash every day!”

protect

verb

To keep someone or something safe.

“Protect your body!”

2 Write a Summary

Write about skin and hair in your own words. Write 15 words or more. Then you can see my example.

💡 Answer these questions

  1. Where is your skin?
  2. What does your skin help you do?
  3. What does your skin stop?
  4. What does your hair do when you are cold?
  5. What does your skin make when you are hot?
  6. How can you protect your body?

✏️ Start like this

  • My skin is …
  • It helps me to …
  • It stops … and …
  • When I am cold, …
  • When I am hot, …
  • Every day, I …
0 / 15 words

⭐ Example Summary

My skin is everywhere on my body. It helps me to touch things and to feel hot and cold. It stops dirt and water getting into my body. Hair grows out of my skin. When I am cold, the hair on my arms and legs stands up. When I am hot, my skin makes sweat. Every day, I wash my skin and hair to protect my body.

3 Presentation Script

Read the script. Practise it. Then present to your class!

Hello!Start

Good morning, everyone! My name is ________. Today I want to talk about my skin and my hair.

Look at this picture. Can you see the skin on this boy’s arm?

👉 Smile. Show the picture of the boy in the rain.
Part 1Skin

First, let’s talk about skin. We have skin everywhere on our body.

Our skin helps us to touch things. It helps us to know when things are hot or cold.

👉 Touch your arm. Say “hot” and “cold” with your hands.
Part 2Skin stops…

Our skin is very useful. It stops dirt getting into our body. It stops water getting into our body, too — when it’s rainy and when we swim.

👉 Point to the picture of the boy in the rain.
Part 3Hair

Next, let’s talk about hair. Hair grows out of our skin.

When we are cold, the hair on our arms and legs stands up. This stops our body getting too cold.

👉 Show the picture. Pretend you are cold: “Brrr!”
Part 4Sweat

And when we are hot, our skin makes sweat. This stops our body getting too hot.

Question for you: When do you sweat? (Wait for answers.) Yes! When we run, play, or when it’s sunny!

👉 Ask the class. Wait. Say “Good answer!”
Part 5Protect

So, how can we protect our body? We can wash every day! Then we get dirt and sweat off our skin and hair.

👉 Show the washing picture. Pretend to wash your hair.
The EndFinish

Remember: our skin and hair help us every day. Let’s wash every day and protect our body!

Thank you for listening! Do you have any questions?

👉 Smile and say “Thank you!”

🌟 Presentation Tips

  • Speak slowly and loudly.
  • Look at your friends, not only at the paper.
  • Point to the pictures when you talk.
  • Smile! 😊
